html:
The State of Israel was declared on 14 May 1948, as British rule in Palestine ended. The next day the armies of Egypt, Transjordan, Syria and Iraq invaded, beginning the first Arab-Israeli war, which ran until armistice agreements in 1949.

The United Nations had voted in November 1947 to split Palestine into a Jewish state and an Arab state, with Jerusalem under international rule. Jewish leaders accepted; Arab leaders rejected the plan, and civil war broke out inside Palestine. David Ben-Gurion read the declaration of independence in Tel Aviv.

Israel's forces held off the invasion and ended the war with more land than the UN plan had given it. Transjordan took the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Egypt held the Gaza Strip; no Arab state of Palestine was formed.

About 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled, an event Palestinians call the Nakba, "the catastrophe". In the following years most Jews of the Arab world left for Israel in the Jewish exodus from Arab lands. The conflict that began here shaped the region for the rest of the century.
